extracted.intended_audience: designers, companies and IP practitioners seeking international registration of industrial designs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules for filing and managing international registrations of industrial designs under the WIPO Hague System, including eligibility, fees, eHague online filing, and lifecycle management (searching, filing, updating, renewal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can use the Hague System
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationals of… Anyone with domicile or habitual residence in… Anyone with a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in… any of the Hague System’s 82 members (referred to as “contracting parties”) – including all countries in the European Union (EU) and the African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) – can use the Hague System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is based on nationality, domicile/habitual residence, or a real and effective industrial/commercial establishment in a contracting party. The page lists 82 members covering 99 countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of designs per international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Registering up to 100 designs in 99 countries by filing a single international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single international application may include up to 100 designs. Use the Hague System to bundle multiple designs for international protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: types and payable currency
rubrics_metrics.description: International design applications are subject to the payment of three types of fees, all payable in Swiss francs (CHF): a basic fee; a publication fee; and a standard designation fee or an individual designation fee for each contracting party where you seek protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic fee example given: 397 CHF for one design; 50 CHF for each additional design in the same application. Publication fee examples: 17 CHF for each reproduction; 150 CHF for each page on which one or more reproductions are shown. Note: standard designation fees follow a three-level structure reflecting the level of examination carried out by the contracting party. See 'Calculate your fees' and 'Fees and payment methods' for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prerequisite national or regional application required
rubrics_metrics.description: Do I need a national or regional application or registration before I can file an international application? No, you do not need a prior national/regional application (unlike, for instance, under the Madrid System).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may file directly under the Hague System without first filing nationally or regionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an international application under the Hague System, applicants can designate as few or as many of those contracting parties as desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are 82 members covering 99 countries; applicants choose which contracting parties to designate for protection and pay designation fees accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifecycle coverage: filing through renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hague System supports you throughout the lifecycle of your designs, from application for protection through to renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional lifecycle actions explicitly supported include: searching protected designs; filing international design applications; managing international design registrations (update, transfer ownership, renunciation, limitation, etc.); and renewing international registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of eHague online services
rubrics_metrics.description: Use eHague to file your international design applications and manage your registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eHague provides online filing and a workbench for management. Resources include 'Filing tutorial and demo of eHague', 'eHague workbench', and 'Strong authentication'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search protected designs before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching protected designs: Check what your competitors are doing by searching existing designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO encourages prior searches of protected designs to inform filing strategy; tools/resources are linked on the page (e.g., Global Design Database).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing reproductions (linked guide): applicants must prepare reproductions of the design(s) according to WIPO guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific 'Preparing reproductions' PDF user guide is provided; follow that guide for acceptable formats, views, and quality for reproductions used in the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including multiple designs in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: Including multiple designs in an international application (linked guide): guidance on how to include multiple designs within the same international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated PDF explains rules and best practices for grouping designs in a single application (e.g., classification, fees, reproductions). Consult that guide when filing more than one design together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fees linked to reproductions/pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication fee: 17 CHF for each reproduction; 150 CHF for each page on which one or more reproductions are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication costs depend on the number of reproductions and pages; plan for these fees when preparing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer support and enquiry handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Hague System Customer Service team is available to answer all your questions and assist you throughout the lifecycle of your international design applications and registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00–18:00 (Geneva time). Use the 'Contact Hague' link for enquiries, email alerts, and other assistance channels (phone number provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and tutorial resources available
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of legal resources and user tools is provided: Hague System legal texts, information notices, Hague System forms, history of Hague Regulations (PDF), user guides, information kit, member profiles, declarations by contracting parties, and tutorials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and practitioners should consult these resources (forms, legal texts, guides, webinars, tutorials) to comply with formal requirements and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard vs individual designation fee distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: International design applications require either a standard designation fee or an individual designation fee for each contracting party where you seek protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard designation fees follow a three-level structure reflecting the level of examination carried out by the contracting party. Check member profiles/declarations for the applicable fee type and examination level of each contracting party.
